cause_check: READ. The -40% is the structural cable de-rate punctuated by a peer's collapse and by Comcast's own decision to break itself up. 2026-04-23 +7.7% to $31.64 on 46.5M shares: the Q1 print, where the market bought 'the pivot is working' (broadband net losses improved 117,000 y/y to -65,000, record wireless adds, Theme Parks EBITDA +33%, Peacock revenue +71%) DESPITE adjusted EPS -27.5%, adjusted EBITDA -16.8% and FCF -28.0% in the same release. 2026-04-24 -12.9% to $27.56 on 65.5M shares: SECTOR, NOT COMPANY - Charter reported Q1 broadband losses and had its worst trading day on record (Deadline: 'Charter Shares Plummet After Broadband Losses'; Barron's: 'Is the Cable Era Over? Charter's Subscriber Slump Reignites Fears of a Fiber and Satellite Threat'; Seeking Alpha: '...dragging down sector peers'); no CMCSA 8-K that day, only the DEF 14A. 2026-06-29 +4.5%: 8-K Ex-99.1 announcing the intention to separate into two public companies via a tax-free spin of NBCUniversal and Sky ~one year out, and PAUSING the buyback. 2026-07-23 -6.8% to $21.92, the 3-year low: the Q2 print. 2026-07-28 +6.1%: breakup/SOTP re-rating plus institutional accumulation (BofA bought 3.78M shares 07-30/31).
path_check: PASSES the numeric guard, FAILS on substance. +12.0% off a 10-day-old low ($21.92 close 2026-07-23; $21.28 intraday 07-24) clears every threshold in the generator. But the low IS the Q2 earnings-day close and the +15.4% bounce since is not dip-buying - it is the market repricing the June 29 breakup announcement. We are LATE to the capitulation and EARLY to a 12-month corporate reorganisation: the worst intersection of the two, and the numeric path guard cannot see it.
spin_adjustment_finding: THE LANE'S HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED - the premise does NOT break, and the error direction is conservative, not inflationary. The generator's price source (yf.Ticker(tk).history(period='3y')['Close']) IS spin-adjusted for Versant. Verified three ways: (1) PRIMARY - Versant Media Group 10-Q Q1-2026, CIK 0002067876, accession 0002067876-26-000027, Note 7 Stockholders' Equity, verbatim: 'The Separation from Comcast was completed on January 2, 2026 ... as of the close of business on the record date of December 16, 2025. Comcast's shareholders of record received one share of Versant Class A common stock ... for every 25 shares of Comcast Class A common stock.' (2) VSNT's first regular-way close was ~$46.63; at 1:25 that is $1.87 per CMCSA share against an unadjusted pre-spin close of $29.88, implying a back-adjustment factor of 28.01/29.88 = 0.9374. (3) IBKR's own pre-2026-01-02 daily bars carry a CONSTANT non-round scaling that solves to 0.93678 - matching the filing-derived 0.9374 to within 0.06% and constant ACROSS ex-dividend dates, so it is a spin factor not a dividend factor - while Yahoo's raw Close shows NO ex-date gap at all (28.01 -> 27.69 across 2025-12-31/2026-01-02, an ordinary market day). Both vendors agree on the pre-spin level (IBKR $28.001 vs Yahoo raw $28.013 on 2025-12-31; $30.455 vs $30.469 on 2025-08-05). CONSEQUENCE: had the series been left unadjusted, pre-spin prices would be 6.3% HIGHER and the naive drawdown would read DEEPER (~-44% vs -40%) - a naive screen would OVER-select this name, not under-select it. The drawdown qualifies for the 35-78% band on any of the three bases. NO P1 DEFECT on the spin axis; retire the concern for the whole spinoff-adjacent cohort.
generator_defects: P1 - MISSING pending_corporate_action GATE. The screen has no field for 'this company has announced that it is splitting itself in two.' CMCSA announced a tax-free spin of NBCUniversal and Sky on 2026-06-29 and paused its buyback the same day. Three consequences the score cannot see: (a) the 'own 3-year high' reference is measured against a materially different asset mix - the $39.75 high included Versant, Sky Germany AND NBCU; two are gone and the third is going, and no price adjustment fixes a FORWARD change in composition; (b) the security you buy is not the security you hold; (c) the buyback, often the main per-share support in a de-rated large cap, can be switched off by the action itself. RECOMMENDATION: parse recent 8-K items 1.01/2.01/8.01 headlines for separation/spin/merger/split language over a trailing 12 months, set a pending_corporate_action flag, and apply a hard score multiplier in the style of the existing factor_costume x 0.30. Sibling of the existing spinoff_orphans generator; can share its corporate-action feed.

P3 - BASIS MISMATCH. The premise is multiple compression, a PRICE concept, but the drawdown is computed on history(period='3y') with auto_adjust=True, a TOTAL-RETURN series. For CMCSA at a 5.4% yield the two diverge materially: -38.2% total-return vs -44.4% price at $24.56, a 6.2-point gap. For a zero-dividend name like TYL they are identical. The metric is therefore not comparable across names and the bias systematically UNDER-ranks high-yielders. Direction is conservative, hence P3 not P1. RECOMMENDATION: compute drawdown_from_3y_high_pct on auto_adjust=False Close (still split- and spin-adjusted) and keep the total-return series only for the P1-4 factor-residual regression, where total return is the correct input.

TIGHTEN - the ice-cube guard is too loose for segmented businesses. CMCSA cleared MIN_REV_CAGR_3Y = -0.02 with a 3-year revenue CAGR of +0.6%, a hair above the floor, while the segment producing 72% of EBITDA was contracting 8%. This is the segment-level-flooring lesson: an aggregate floor hides mix erosion. RECOMMENDATION: where segment data exists, fail a name whose largest-EBITDA segment is in revenue decline regardless of the consolidated CAGR.
edge_explainer: The decisive fact is one line in the Q2 8-K: DOMESTIC BROADBAND REVENUE $6,280M vs $6,649M, DOWN 5.5%, and Comcast's own explanation is 'lower average rates AND a decline in the number of domestic broadband customers' - both terms of the product are negative. Subscribers -1.7% (28,486k vs 28,989k), revenue -5.5%, so ARPU is down ~3.9%. Residential Connectivity & Platforms generates $6.45bn of the company's $8.90bn of quarterly adjusted EBITDA - 72% - and it is shrinking 8% a year with margins down 160bps. MODE B, the pivot's own evidence turned against it: the broadband pivot deliberately trades price for volume, and Comcast has now run the experiment twice - Q1-2026 net losses -65,000 (a 117,000 y/y IMPROVEMENT), Q2-2026 net losses -167,000 (only a 34,000 improvement). The improvement collapsed from 117k to 34k in one quarter while the price giveaway deepened. Crudely: ~3.9% of ARPU is ~$255M of forgone quarterly broadband revenue, and it bought 34,000 subscribers of y/y improvement worth ~$9M of quarterly revenue. The counterfactual is unknowable and management offers none, but the ratio is trending the wrong way. HONESTY READ: the marketed takeaway is 'our strategic pivot in broadband is gaining traction' and the lead highlight bullet is 'Net Losses Improving by 34,000 Year-over-Year'; the data underneath shows the RATE of improvement fell by two thirds q/q while the revenue cost rose. Every input is in the segment tables - this is emphasis, not concealment. REVIEW_FLAG on emphasis, not ELEVATE: honestly disclosed bad news is CLEAN and re-detecting it is not the product. But the direction of the second derivative is the alpha-relevant read and it is the one the release does not frame. WHAT YOU ARE ACTUALLY BUYING: not the company in the screen's price history, and not the one you would own in a year. Versant spun 2026-01-02; Sky Germany sold 2026-05-31; on 2026-06-29 Comcast announced its intention to spin NBCUniversal AND Sky into a second public company ~one year out (Angelakis returns as CEO of the connectivity RemainCo, Cavanagh runs NBCU), restructured its near-term maturities through cash tender offers across thirteen note series in May-June, and PAUSED the buyback. The lane brief described CMCSA as 'post-Versant-spin RemainCo' - it is not; the large separation is AHEAD. THE UNANSWERABLE QUESTION: verified capital structure at 2026-06-30 is gross debt $90,381M ($84,264M long-term + $6,117M current) against cash $7,661M + ST investments $17M = NET DEBT $82,703M; 3,570M diluted shares at $24.56 = $87.7bn cap and EV $170.4bn; H1 adjusted EBITDA $16,831M annualises to ~$33.5bn, so 5.1x EV/EBITDA and 2.47x net leverage - fine consolidated. But post-split, connectivity carries ~$31.9bn of DECLINING EBITDA and NBCU ~$5bn of growing EBITDA; if the debt follows the cash flow, which it will, the connectivity RemainCo becomes a ~2.5x-levered melting asset. The Form 10 is not filed. The allocation is UNVERIFIABLE and it is the swing factor. THE SIBLING SPIN IS THE READ-THROUGH: VSNT traded when-issued ~$46-47, opened regular-way ~$46.6, and is $36.82 today - -22.6% from its own high, having fallen 13.0%/10.6%/8.2% on 2026-01-05/06/07 as index funds and mandate-constrained holders dumped a small-cap media stub; the parallel tier-4 lane courts it as FORCED_SELL_DOWNGRADE for exactly that reason, and the same mechanism applies to a much larger NBCU stub in 2027. CLAIM CHECKS: 'Pro forma revenue +4.7%' is TRUE AND MATERIALLY INCOMPLETE - on the identical pro-forma basis adjusted EBITDA fell 5.3%, and 2026 carries an unusually heavy sports slate (Milan Cortina + Super Bowl LX in Q1, FIFA World Cup in Q2) that inflates revenue and barely moves EBITDA (Media revenue +25.3%, or +15.6% ex-World-Cup, converts to Media EBITDA +3.7%). 'Best wireless quarter ever, 448,000 adds, 10.2M lines' is CONFIRMED and genuinely good, wireless service revenue +14.2% - but it is $1,007M against $6,280M of broadband, so the whole wireless business is 16% the size of the line it is meant to defend, and Domestic Convergence revenue (the actual strategic unit) is still -3.2%. 'Peacock profitable for the first time' is CONFIRMED at +$189M EBITDA - and it is going to the other company. Theme Parks revenue +2.7% but EBITDA -5.1%, with management conceding 'near-term softness'. Capex +8.3% with connectivity capex +19.9% - spending more to shrink. VALUATION: ~6.7x FY26E adjusted EPS, 5.1x EV/EBITDA, ~14.8% FCF yield, 5.42% dividend at a ~36% payout. Statistically very cheap - which is exactly what a value trap looks like, and the burden of proof is on the denominator. THE SCREEN'S FRAME IS MISAPPLIED: 'quality-at-own-history-discount' presumes a fallen compounder, and the 69% gross margin that cleared the quality gate is an artifact of cable's cost structure (programming is the only major cost above the line), not a proxy for a moat - and the moat is precisely what fibre overbuild, FWA and LEO are eroding, as Charter demonstrated to the whole sector in one session on 2026-04-24. E[FV] $26.05 = +6.1% price, ~+11.5% total with the dividend, against a 35% probability of a 23% drawdown to $19. Under the fairly-paid-risk doctrine the bar is fairness verified PLUS tails bounded; fairness is roughly verified but a levered connectivity RemainCo against declining EBITDA is precisely an unbounded tail. REJECT.
